title.narrative: Emergency response to improve food security for vulnerable people affected by flooding in the Logone et Chari department of Cameroon

description.narrative: Cameroon's Far North region is facing multiple crises, making it the most vulnerable to climatic hazards combined with multi-faceted conflicts. The results of the latest analysis of the food and nutritional security situation (March, 2024) show that 3 departments (Logone et Chari, Mayo-Sava and Mayo-Tsanaga) are in crisis phase, and the 3 other departments are in stress phase, with the possibility of the situation deteriorating if effective and coordinated action is not taken. The current floods have further worsened the food security situation. Prior to the floods, the departments of Logone et Chari and Mayo-Danay were already registering 334,645 food insecure people (phase 3 and above). The floods affected a further 356,730 people, with the highest numbers in Logone et Chari (156,294 people) and Mayo-Danay (198,174 people), who were still in the lean season. These people also saw their livelihoods affected. Satellite monitoring of flooding by the FAO from 09/16 to 09/30, 2024 showed that flooded crop areas represented 64.25% of sown areas in Logone et Chari and 31.99% in Mayo-Danay (FAO, Flood monitoring tool). Overall, nearly half of all crops were flooded in both departments, but the deterioration was more marked in Logone et Chari. These flooding effects, combined with prevalent food insecurity, are leading households to adopt negative and more complex coping strategies, worsening the level of severity of food and nutritional security.With this in mind, FAO has geographically targeted its response in the Logone et Chari department. The aim of this intervention is to help cover the food needs and emergency production of own food of vulnerable populations affected by the floods. This support will also enable predominantly agricultural households to avoid developing emergency livelihood strategies. These include selling the last reproductive females or begging for food or money to buy food. In addition to cash, the food security of beneficiary households will be improved by the emergency agricultural revival of short-cycle, quick-impact off-season crops, taking advantage of the availability of water and sediment from the floods.The FAO will target a total of 9,200 people, or an average of 1,667 vulnerable households affected by the floods. They will receive a two-month cash transfer accompanied by a short-term emergency production kit, enabling them to consume their own highly nutritious produce from the third month onwards. In the short term, households' food and nutritional security will be improved by the level of their consumption score and their dietary diversity. In the medium term, household livelihoods will be protected and restored.
